description: The reader's windows: only the app commands the UI calls (open a document through the dialog, unlock it, its pages, what its Properties dialog shows, picking another PDF, or several, to take pages from, giving one to a document as a source, merging them with it into a new file, saving a copy of a change a signature refused, choosing a folder to write files into and writing a document's parts there or to one file, its edits (applying, undoing and redoing them, saying whether the window holds unsaved ones, and that a quit asking about them was cancelled), dropping tiles it no longer wants, closing it, taking the files the OS asked it to open before it was ready, the recent files by id, the app's preferences and the system's reduce-motion setting, Settings › Graphics (what this start runs with, and the crash-loop notice, once), Restart now and Settings › About's View licences, and its windows and tabs: a new window, moving a tab to another window, the list of windows, the window's title, taking the tabs moved to it before it was ready, a tab's drag out of or between windows, and the last session: reporting its tabs, taking its restored tabs, after an unexpected quit the tabs to choose from and reopening the chosen ones, opening one, and locating a missing one; the native menus: its commands' state, closing the window, quitting, saving a copy of one of its documents, and printing one: the OS's print dialog over pages the engine renders, and stopping it; saving a document's edits: planning the save, saving in place or as a new file, and reloading a document whose file another app changed; updates: their status, Check now, the Automatic updates switch and the channel, a new anonymous ID, Restart to update and its two pages; crash reports: the question after a crash and its answer, the Send crash reports switch and its sample, and the page's own uncaught errors) and listening for the open requests' and tabs' events, the engine's restart and failure events, the events of a file that changed on disk, the preferences' changes, the crash question's event, and the questions asked before closing or quitting with unsaved edits. core:default is not granted; each core permission is named (ADR 0008 §6).
